name: 香格里拉
description: Shangri-La sits at 3,280 meters on the edge of the Tibetan Plateau in northwest Yunnan province, and is the only prefecture in China officially renamed after James Hilton's fictional utopia. The city is a working Tibetan-Buddhist town, not a museum: monks in maroon robes walk to morning prayers at Songzanlin Monastery (the largest Gelug monastery in Yunnan, often called the 'Little Potala Palace'), and yak herders still graze their animals in surrounding summer pastures. Foreign visitors came here in waves after Yunnan was named in The New York Times' 52 Places list for 2026 (January 2026), and Diqing Airport added new routes through summer 2026. The old town — Dukezong — has a 21-meter prayer wheel (one of the largest in the world) and a maze of cobblestone alleys that flood with butter-tea light in winter. Two realities every visitor should know: altitude hits hard the first 24 hours (headaches, mild nausea — common and manageable), and the city gates both Pudacuo National Park and the starting point of Tiger Leaping Gorge, so most travelers use Shangri-La as a base, not a single-day stop.
highlights: Songzanlin Monastery - Yunnan's largest Tibetan Buddhist monastery (Little Potala)
Pudacuo National Park - First national park in mainland China (UNESCO Biosphere)
Dukezong Old Town - 1,300-year-old Tibetan quarter with the giant prayer wheel
Tiger Leaping Gorge - One of the deepest canyons on Earth (3,900m drop)
Napa Lake Wetland - Seasonal lake with yaks and black-necked cranes (winter)
Meili Snow Mountains - Sacred Kawagebo peak (6,740m), from Deqin 2.5h north

climate.tips: UV is extreme year-round — SPF 50 and lip balm are non-negotiable. Summer (July-August) brings most rain; the greenest landscapes but also landslide risk on mountain roads. Spring and autumn have the clearest views of Meili Snow Mountains. Winter (December-February) is dry, sunny during the day, and brutally cold after sunset — temperatures drop 15-20C from day to night. Daytime UV at 3,280m is roughly 40% stronger than at sea level.

attractions.name: 松赞林寺
attractions.description: Founded in 1679 and rebuilt after 1959 damage, Songzanlin is the largest Tibetan-Buddhist Gelug monastery in Yunnan, housing around 700 monks. The five-story main hall is gilded in copper and gold and sits at the foot of Foping Mountain, modeled loosely on Lhasa's Potala Palace. Visitors typically spend 2-3 hours: the front temple (open to tourists), the upper meditation halls (closed to visitors), and the surrounding lake that reflects the monastery in still weather.
attractions.address: 5 km north of Shangri-La Old Town, on National Road G214
attractions.openingHours: 08:00-17:00 (last entry 16:30); closed during major Buddhist holidays
highlights: Lamasery museum of Tibetan Buddhist art
Sky burial site behind the monastery (closed to visitors)
Morning prayer chanting around 06:00 — open to outside viewing
attractions.tips: Arrive before 09:00 to see monks entering for morning prayers (chanting audible from outside the tourist entrance). The sky burial platform behind the monastery is closed to non-Tibetans; please respect this. Photography of monks requires permission. Take Bus 3 from the old town (¥1) or a taxi (¥20). The on-site yak butter tea is mid-quality — better in Dukezong Old Town.

attractions.name: 普达措国家公园
attractions.description: Opened in 2007 as China's first national park at the mainland level, Pudacuo protects 1,300 km² of alpine wetlands, fir forests, and three lakes (Bita Hai, Shudu Hai, and Duocuo) at 3,500-4,000m elevation. The park's Shudu Lake and Bita Lake host rare species including the Yunnan snub-nosed monkey, black-necked cranes (winter migrants), and the endangered Yunnan green pea. Most visitors ride the park's mandatory sightseeing bus between three viewing areas and walk the 4 km boardwalk at Shudu Lake.
attractions.address: Shudu Lake entrance: 22 km east of Shangri-La Old Town
attractions.openingHours: 08:00-16:00 (last bus departs 14:00); closed in severe winter snow
highlights: Shudu Lake 4 km boardwalk (no altitude gain)
Bita Lake viewing platform (shorter walk, deeper water)
Yunnan snub-nosed monkey habitat (very rarely seen)
attractions.tips: Take the park's mandatory sightseeing bus — private cars stopped being allowed in 2019. Altitude here (3,500-4,000m) is significantly higher than Shangri-La Old Town (3,280m) — bring altitude pills, water, and snacks; do NOT hike the optional 1 km climb to Militang Pasture unless you've acclimatized for 2+ days. The wooden boardwalk is the safest route. November is best for fall colors, May for wildflowers.

attractions.name: 独克宗古城
attractions.description: Built over 1,300 years ago as a stop on the ancient Tea-Horse Road, Dukezong means 'Moonlight City' in Tibetan. The old town covers 3 square km of cobblestone alleys, whitewashed Tibetan houses, and a central square dominated by the Guishan Park giant prayer wheel — 21 meters tall, weighing 60 tons, requiring multiple monks to rotate. A 2014 fire destroyed much of the original quarter; the reconstruction was completed in 2016 and rebuilt with concrete fireproofing but preserved the street plan.
highlights: Night market on the main square (Tibetan clothing, dried yak meat)
attractions.tips: Spin the giant prayer wheel clockwise (same direction as Tibetan Buddhist practice) — etiquette matters, locals do notice. Many restaurants and cafes have rooftop terraces with views toward Foping Mountain. The night market on the lower square sells dried yak meat, barley wine, and Tibetan hats; bargaining is expected but keep it light. Avoid the mass-tourist restaurants on the main square; walk two alleys in for better food.

attractions.name: 虎跳峡
attractions.description: One of the deepest gorges on Earth: the Jinsha River (upper Yangtze) drops 3,900 meters between Haba Snow Mountain (5,396m) and Yulong Snow Mountain (5,596m) over a 16-km stretch. The gorge is named after a legend of a tiger leaping across at its narrowest point (about 30m wide at the river level). The classic 2-day trek runs the 28-km high trail along the north side with basic guesthouses at Halfway and Tina's Guesthouse; the lower road is now paved and accessible by minibus for a same-day view from the river.
attractions.address: Qiaotou Town, 105 km south of Shangri-La (1.5h by bus)
highlights: Upper Bend viewpoint (best photo spot, 1h from start)
Halfway Guesthouse (best mid-trek stop, owned by local Naxi family)
Tina's Guesthouse (most international; meets trek end)
attractions.tips: The 2-day trek is moderate fitness, NOT dangerous — switchbacks not ladders. Start early (before 09:00) from Qiaotou to avoid afternoon rain. Avoid the trek in July-August (heavy rain, landslide risk on the trail). You DO NOT need a guide, just the ¥65 ticket at the trailhead. Bring 2L water and rain gear. From Shangri-La: take the Lijiang-bound bus and ask to be dropped at Qiaotou (~2 hours).

attractions.name: 纳帕海
attractions.description: Napa Hai (literally 'Napa Sea') is a seasonal lake and wetland 8 km north of Shangri-La Old Town. From June to September it floods into a 30 km² lake; from October to May it becomes a high-altitude grassland grazed by yaks, horses, and the endangered black-necked cranes (which migrate here from Tibet for winter). The wetland is officially protected and a popular spot for horse riding — most guesthouses in town can arrange a half-day ride for ¥150-300.
attractions.address: 8 km north of Shangri-La Old Town
attractions.recommendedVisitTime: Half day (3-4 hours including horse ride)
highlights: Tibetan village homestays in nearby Yi cun
attractions.tips: October-March is the dry season — grassland, fewer mosquitoes, and the cranes are here. June-September is the lake season — beautiful but bring mosquito repellent. Horse riding is best arranged through your guesthouse, NOT through touts at the entrance. The road here is paved but unlit — don't drive back after 19:00.

attractions.name: 梅里雪山
attractions.description: From Deqin County 2.5 hours north of Shangri-La, the Meili range offers the closest road-accessible view of Kawagebo — the sacred 6,740m peak that has never been summited. Kawagebo is one of only two 6,000m+ peaks in the world that has never been climbed (the other is K2's sister). The best viewpoint is the Feilai Si pass, which sees 'sunlit golden peak' (sunrise hitting Kawagebo) only ~30 days per year, mostly October-November. Most visitors stay one night in Deqin and return the next morning.
attractions.address: Feilai Si viewpoint, 5 km west of Deqin Town
attractions.openingHours: Open 24 hours; viewpoint best at sunrise
highlights: Mingyong Glacier (one of the world's lowest-altitude glaciers at 2,700m)
attractions.tips: Yubeng village has been CLOSED to foreign tourists multiple times in recent years for permit reasons — confirm at your guesthouse 1 week before. The Feilai Si pass has only ~30 'golden peak' sunrise days/year; check the previous night's weather. Drive yourself or take Deqin-bound bus from Shangri-La Bus Station (3 daily, ~3 hours, ¥60). Bring heavy layers even in summer — Deqin sits at 3,550m.

attractions.name: 里塘寺 (天宝雪山脚)
attractions.description: Litong Temple is a small Gelug monastery at the foot of Tiansheng Snow Mountain (also called Haba Snow Mountain's southern flank), 30 km north of Shangri-La. The monastery is small (around 30 monks) but the surrounding area combines Tibetan Buddhist farmhouses, a natural hot spring pool, and the dramatic Tiansheng Bridge limestone formation. Less crowded than Songzanlin but a better feel for everyday Tibetan religious life.
attractions.address: Luoji Village, 30 km north of Shangri-La Old Town
highlights: Tiansheng Bridge natural limestone arch (45 min walk)
attractions.tips: Reach via rented car (~¥400 round trip) or shared van from the old town. The hot spring is functional but basic — bring your own towel and flip-flops. The natural bridge is a moderate 45-minute uphill hike from the village. Respect monastery photography rules — ask before photographing monks.

attractions.name: 香格里拉动物园
attractions.description: A small zoo operated by the Diqing Forestry Bureau, focused on native highland species rather than international animals. Notable residents: yaks, Tibetan mastiffs, snow leopards (in cold-climate enclosures), brown bears, and black-necked cranes. Better than its modest size suggests — well-maintained enclosures and very low crowds. Good option for a half-day with children or on weather-restricted days.
attractions.address: 8 km north of Shangri-La Old Town, on National Road G214
highlights: Snow leopard enclosure (rare sighting in China)
attractions.tips: Take Bus 3 from the old town (¥1) or taxi (~¥15). Pair with Napa Lake wetland on the same day — both are north of town. Feeding animals is forbidden. The bird-watching area is best in early morning.

attractions.name: 哈巴雪山
attractions.description: Haba Xue Shan (5,396m) is one of the most accessible 5,000m+ peaks for climbers without technical experience — the standard summit route is non-technical scrambling, often attempted as a 2-day climb with a guide. The mountain also has lower trails to Black Lake (Heihai) and Tiger Leaping Gorge trailhead. The village at the base (Haba Cun) is small Naxi and far less touristy than its famous southern neighbor Yulong Xue Shan.
attractions.address: Haba Village, 120 km south of Shangri-La (2.5h by bus)
attractions.tips: Summit attempts should be booked 7+ days ahead through a registered guide (Yunnan Mountaineering Association certified). Off-season (November-March) summit attempt is unsafe — snow too deep. For Black Lake only, no permit needed but bring altitude meds, 2L water, and warm layers even in summer. The Haba Village guesthouses are basic but warm (~¥80/night including dinner).

attractions.name: 迪庆藏族自治州博物馆
attractions.description: Free museum in the new town covering Diqing's Tibetan cultural history, geology, and ecological zones. Three floors: ground floor (Tibetan ethnic culture, religious objects), second floor (natural history, fossils, animals of the Hengduan Mountains), third floor (rotating photography exhibits). English signage is functional but patchy; the building itself — modern Tibetan architectural style — is worth a quick photo.
attractions.address: Changzheng Avenue, Shangri-La New Town (15 min walk from old town)
attractions.tips: Pair with a Songzanlin morning visit — museum opens at 09:00, monastery at 08:00. Bring your passport (free admission requires it). The third-floor photo exhibits change every 3-6 months. Good on a rainy day.

attractions.name: 白鸡寺
attractions.description: Small hilltop nunnery overlooking Dukezong Old Town, founded in the early 18th century. The temple houses around 30 nuns and offers the best panoramic view of Shangri-La Old Town and Foping Mountain behind Songzanlin. A 15-minute uphill walk from the old town. Quieter than Songzanlin and rarely visited by tour groups; a good place to talk with the nuns if you speak Mandarin.
attractions.address: Northern edge of Dukezong Old Town, Shangri-La
highlights: Best panoramic view of old town and Foping Mountain
attractions.tips: Walk uphill from the northern corner of the old town (20 min, well-signed). Sunrise is the best time — soft golden light on Foping Mountain behind Songzanlin. Modest dress (covered shoulders and knees). The small tea house at the base sells yak butter tea at honest prices.

attractions.name: 巴拉格宗
attractions.description: A 3-hour drive north of Shangri-La, Balagezong is a Tibetan village in a deep canyon reachable only since 2008 (the village was cut off for centuries). The road itself is dramatic — switchbacks carved into cliffs. The destination: Bala village (1,000-year-old Tibetan settlement), an eco-village resort with monastery, hot springs, and views of 5,545m peaks. Worth it for travelers who have a spare full day and want to see Diqing's most dramatic landscape.
attractions.address: Bala Village, 110 km north of Shangri-La (3h by bus)
attractions.tips: Book a day tour from a guesthouse in Shangri-La (~¥400 incl. transport and lunch). The 3-hour bus ride is the rough part — roads narrow and switchback-heavy if you get carsick. Bring altitude pills; the canyon floor is 1,800m and rises sharply. Best May-October; avoid winter (snow closes roads).

restaurants.name: 塔玛瑞藏餐厅
restaurants.description: Long-standing Tibetan restaurant in Dukezong Old Town serving yak meat dishes, butter tea, and tsampa (roasted barley flour). Warm interior with low lighting; a reliable choice for first-time Tibetan food.
restaurants.address: Dukezong Old Town, near the giant prayer wheel
restaurants.tips: Try the yak meat momos (dumplings, ¥45) — generous filling. The butter tea is salty, not sweet — that's authentic Tibetan style. Arrive before 19:00 for dinner — fills up with tour groups by 19:30.

restaurants.name: 绿松石云来餐厅
restaurants.description: Higher-end Tibetan-Yunnanese fusion restaurant in a converted Tibetan house. Known for yak steak and matsutake mushroom dishes in season (June-October). Garden seating in summer.
restaurants.address: Dukezong Old Town, north side alleys
restaurants.tips: Reservation recommended for summer matsutake season (July-September). The matsutake fried rice is the standout. Card payment accepted (rare in old town); cash still faster.

restaurants.name: 达孔厨房
restaurants.description: Casual family-run Tibetan kitchen with authentic home-cooked dishes and friendly English-speaking owner (Nam, trained as a guide). A good value option for travelers wanting to try multiple Tibetan dishes without ordering hot pot.
restaurants.address: Dukezong Old Town, near the Tibetan handicraft market
restaurants.tips: Ask for the 'Tibetan combo' if you want to try multiple dishes. The yak yogurt is genuinely sour — that's correct, not spoiled. English menu available. Owner Nam can arrange guide contacts for Meili/Tiger Leaping.

restaurants.name: 静河咖啡
restaurants.description: Foreign-owned Tibetan courtyard cafe serving proper espresso, Western breakfasts (until 11:00), and Tibetan lunch options. The best place in town to get a proper coffee and reliable Wi-Fi for video calls. Owner is responsive to dietary restrictions.
restaurants.address: Dukezong Old Town, near the south gate
restaurants.tips: Best Wi-Fi reliability in town for video calls. Get there before 09:00 for breakfast — only 4 tables in the courtyard. Owner can connect you with local guides for off-the-beaten-path trips.

restaurants.name: 酥油茶馆
restaurants.description: Authentic working-class Tibetan tea house with no English menu and minimal signage — most tourists don't find it. Local Tibetan families come here for breakfast (po cha, tsampa, yak cheese). Prices are honest, atmosphere is genuine.
restaurants.address: Dukezong Old Town, west side alleys (off the main square)
restaurants.tips: Sit where locals sit (avoid empty plastic chairs). Point to what you want if you don't read Tibetan script. Try the po cha — it's salty, that's correct. Closing time 13:00 sharp. Bring small bills.

restaurants.name: 云上烤屋
restaurants.description: Open-air barbecue joint with great lamb skewers (yang rou chuan) and grilled mushrooms. Locals' favorite for evening drinking. The cumin-spiced lamb ribs are the standout. No menu in English — picture menu on the wall.
restaurants.address: Near the night market, Dukezong Old Town
restaurants.tips: After 19:00 the night market crowd arrives — get there by 18:30. Order lamb ribs (¥80) and at least 10 lamb skewers. Cash or WeChat Pay only. The mushroom skewers (¥3) in summer are excellent with matsutake.

restaurants.name: 香格里拉厨房
restaurants.description: Upscale hotel restaurant in Shangri-La Old Town serving refined Yunnanese dishes with strong wine list. Popular for special occasions; the truffle-oil infused yak steak and the matsutake chicken soup are signature. Reservations recommended weekends.
restaurants.address: Banyan Tree Ring Road, Dukezong Old Town
restaurants.tips: Pair a Yunnan highland red (¥180/bottle) with the yak steak. Book 1 day ahead for weekends. Card accepted. Dress code smart-casual — no hiking boots.

restaurants.name: 拉萨面馆
restaurants.description: Cheap, fast Tibetan noodle shop across from the old town bus station. Locals' lunch spot. The thukpa (Tibetan noodle soup) and the hand-pulled beef noodle bowl are both excellent at ¥25. No English menu.
restaurants.address: Across from Shangri-La Bus Station, 3-min walk from Dukezong south gate
restaurants.tips: Lunch rush 12:00-13:00 — get there before noon or after 13:30. Cash only. Sit at the long shared table — that's how locals eat. The sweet rice (dresi, ¥15) is a good breakfast if you arrive before 09:00.

restaurants.name: 雪山咖啡馆
restaurants.description: Rooftop cafe on a renovated Tibetan house with views over Dukezong Old Town and toward Foping Mountain. Better for coffee and sunset than for full meals — but the yak butter latte is unique.
restaurants.address: Dukezong Old Town, near Baijisi Temple (north side)
restaurants.tips: Sunset is roughly 19:30 in summer, 18:00 in winter. Get there 30 min before sunset for a good table. Cold evenings — they have blankets. Card payment accepted.

restaurants.name: 纳帕草原烤羊
restaurants.description: Tibetan grassland-style whole lamb roast experience in a Napa Lake grassland tent. You get a whole roasted lamb, tsampa, butter tea, and Tibetan dance performance. Per-person pricing if you don't have 8+ guests is not offered — bring a group or join one. Best with travelers you've met at your guesthouse.
restaurants.address: Napa Lake grassland, 8 km north of Shangri-La Old Town
restaurants.tips: Most guesthouses can pair you with other travelers to share a lamb. Cold in winter — book the tent with the fire pit. Combine with a morning horse ride at Napa Lake. Transport included in most arrangements (~¥200 total).

restaurants.name: 热地咖啡面包房
restaurants.description: Foreign-run bakery serving real sourdough bread, proper croissants, and espresso. Excellent cinnamon rolls and almond croissants. Small seating area, mostly takeaway. Open early (07:30) — best breakfast in town for Western travelers.
restaurants.address: Just outside Dukezong Old Town, near the south bus station
restaurants.tips: Croissants often sell out by 10:00. Buy 2-3 to keep for packed lunches. Cash or WeChat Pay only. Can pre-order bread for Tiger Leaping Gorge trek the day before.

restaurants.name: 老藏家餐厅
restaurants.description: Small family-run Tibetan restaurant near Songzanlin Monastery serving the kind of food monks actually eat — simpler, saltier, more authentic than the old town options. Specializes in butter tea (the proper salty kind) and yak meat stew.
restaurants.address: Near Songzanlin Monastery entrance, 5 km north of Shangri-La Old Town
restaurants.tips: Pair with a Songzanlin morning visit — arrive at the monastery at 08:00, walk down for lunch by 11:30. The Tibetan barley pancakes (¥20) are the standout. English menu available.

hotels.name: 环酒店
hotels.description: Top luxury option in Dukezong Old Town, with Tibetan-style courtyard suites, indoor pool, and spa. Best for special occasions.
hotels.address: Banyan Tree Ring Road, Dukezong Old Town
hotels.tips: Book at least 2 weeks ahead in summer. Western breakfast included. The indoor pool helps acclimatization for altitude.

hotels.name: 香格里拉大酒店
hotels.description: International 5-star resort in the new town with mountain views, large rooms, and full business amenities.
hotels.tips: Request mountain-view room at booking (extra ¥200 but worth it). Free shuttle to old town.

hotels.name: 古城庭院客栈
hotels.description: Renovated Tibetan courtyard inn with wooden rooms and rooftop terrace. Best mid-range option in the old town.
hotels.address: Dukezong Old Town, near Guishan Park
hotels.tips: Book courtyard rooms — interior rooms are darker. The rooftop is closed after 22:00 (Tibetan quiet hours).

hotels.name: 阿如精品酒店
hotels.description: Small boutique hotel with Tibetan-modern fusion design and friendly English-speaking staff. Good value for the location.
hotels.tips: Smaller rooms — request king-size if traveling as a couple. They can arrange guides for Meili/Tiger Leaping with advance notice.

hotels.name: 藏家家庭旅馆
hotels.description: Authentic Tibetan family-run guesthouse — basic but warm and culturally immersive. Family speaks some English.
hotels.address: Dukezong Old Town, near Diqing Museum
hotels.tips: Cold in winter — they provide extra yak-wool blankets. Shared bathroom. Cash only.

hotels.name: 香格里拉青年旅舍
hotels.description: Clean dorm-style hostel with mixed Western/Tibetan atmosphere. Best place to find trekking partners for Tiger Leaping Gorge.
hotels.tips: Dorms are co-ed by floor. Lockers provided (bring own lock). Common kitchen is well-equipped.

hotels.name: 松赞林小屋
hotels.description: Quiet lodge near Songzanlin Monastery with monastery views from upper rooms. Best for early-morning monastery visits without driving in.
hotels.tips: Best for photographers — sunrise shots of the monastery are 5 min walk. Limited dining options nearby.

hotels.name: 高原背包客栈
hotels.description: Basic backpacker inn with shared kitchen and laundry. Older facilities but cheapest reliable option.
hotels.tips: Hot water is solar — best morning or evening. Pickup service from bus station.

hotels.name: 藏式碉楼酒店
hotels.description: Stays inside a renovated Tibetan stone fortress — thick walls keep rooms cool in summer, warm in winter. Unique cultural stay.
hotels.address: Outside Dukezong, 2 km from old town
highlights: Sleep inside a real Tibetan fortress
hotels.tips: Book a fortress room, not the modern annex. Cultural classes (Tibetan incense making, tsampa) bookable through hotel.

hotels.name: 雪域酒店
hotels.description: Simple, clean mid-range hotel in the new town. Reliable for business travelers on a budget.
hotels.tips: Request non-smoking floor. Old town is 15 min walk downhill.

hotels.name: 高原养生温泉酒店
hotels.description: Resort hotel with natural hot spring pools — the altitude-healing angle is real; many guests feel altitude effects ease after a hot spring soak. Large property with multiple pools.
hotels.address: 8 km north of Shangri-La Old Town, near Napa Lake
hotels.tips: Outdoor pools only warm enough May-October. Stay minimum 2 nights — gives time for altitude adjustment. Transport from old town included.

hotels.name: 草甸木屋
hotels.description: Wooden cabins on the Napa Lake grassland edge. Genuine grassland experience — wake up to yaks grazing outside your window. Cold in winter.
hotels.tips: Closed November-March (winter freeze). Bring layers — grassland nights drop to 0C even in August. No Wi-Fi.

transport.byAir: Diqing Shangri-La Airport (DIG) — 5 km from old town. Direct flights from Kunming (1h, ~¥800), Chengdu (2h, ~¥1,500), Shanghai (4h, ~¥2,500), Lhasa (2h, ~¥2,000), and seasonal Beijing (3h). Airport to old town: taxi ¥30, Bus 3 ¥1. Summer 2026 added direct flights from Guangzhou and Chongqing.
transport.byTrain: Lijiang-Shangri-La high-speed rail opened 2023: Lijiang to Shangri-La in 1h 20min, ~¥80. From Kunming via Lijiang: ~5 hours total. The Shangri-La Railway Station is 8 km from old town; taxi ¥25 or Bus 1 ¥1.
transport.byBus: From Lijiang: 4-5 hours, ¥72, frequent departures (every 30 min from Lijiang Bus Station). From Kunming: 10-12 hours, ¥250, overnight buses available. Shangri-La Bus Station is 10 min walk from Dukezong south gate.
transport.localTransport: Old town is walkable. For Napa Lake (8 km north) and Songzanlin (5 km north): Bus 3 (¥1), shared van (¥5), or taxi (¥20-30). For Pudacuo (22 km east): tourist shuttle from old town (¥30 one-way) or taxi (~¥120 round trip). For Tiger Leaping Gorge (105 km south): tour operators in old town offer day trips (~¥400).
transport.tips: Diqing Airport flights can be cancelled in winter due to snow — book buffer days if flying out in December-February. The Lijiang-Shangri-La high-speed rail is more reliable than flying in winter. Self-driving from Lijiang: 4h, road is paved (last 30 km to Tiger Leaping Gorge is winding).

payment.cashVsCard: Old town shops and most restaurants are CASH ONLY or WeChat/Alipay only. ATMs at ICBC and Agricultural Bank branches on Changzheng Avenue. Visa/MasterCard accepted at the larger hotels (Banyan Tree, Shangri-La Resort) and a few upmarket restaurants. Mobile pay (Alipay/WeChat) is now the dominant payment method.
payment.wechatAlipay: Foreign visitors can use Alipay (Tap to Pay with Visa/Mastercard) since 2024. WeChat Pay also works with foreign Visa cards (slower setup, requires Chinese mobile number). Bank of China in the new town supports foreign card cash withdrawal at better rates than the airport ATM.
payment.tips: Carry ¥500-1,000 in small bills (¥10/20/50) for old town restaurants and markets. For hotels and tours, mobile pay works reliably. Avoid airport currency exchange — better rates in town.
atmLocations: ICBC ATM (Changzheng Avenue, near old town)
Agricultural Bank ATM (north end of Changzheng Ave)

culturalTips: Climbing the prayer wheel: always go CLOCKWISE (Buddhist direction). Locals do notice if you go the wrong way.
Monastery etiquette: remove hats, speak quietly, no pointing feet at Buddha statues when sitting, ask before photographing monks.
Sky burial sites: visible from trails but closed to non-Tibetan visitors. Respect the closure — not a curiosity, a religious practice.
Tibetan greetings: 'Tashi Delek' (བཀྲ་ཤིས་བདེ་ལེགས) is the standard 'hello'. A slight bow with hands together is polite.
Yak butter tea is savory, not sweet. If your host offers it, sip at least once — refusing can offend.
Altitude: 3,280m at the old town, 3,500-4,000m at Pudacuo. Take it easy for the first 24 hours — short walks, no alcohol, lots of water.
Yak and dog safety: Tibetan mastiffs guarding monasteries look intimidating — DO NOT touch them, don't make eye contact, walk past calmly.
Photography: ask before photographing monks or Tibetan families. Many refuse — respect that. Landscapes and architecture are fine.
Donations at monasteries: cash in the donation box is welcomed; ¥10-20 is reasonable. Better than nothing — better than too much.
Haggling at the night market: expected, but keep it light and friendly. Heavy bargaining with Tibetan vendors is culturally off.

emergencyContacts.englishSupport: Diqing Foreign Affairs Office: +86 887 822 2800 (limited English; better for guides/translators)
emergencyContacts.mainHospital: Diqing People's Hospital (8 km from old town, taxi ¥25). Has English-speaking staff at the international clinic on the 2nd floor.
emergencyContacts.embassies: For emergency embassy assistance, call the 24/7 Chinese MFA hotline: +86 10 6561 2300.

quickFacts.ethnicGroups: Tibetan (45%), Han (35%), Naxi, Yi, Bai, Lisu
quickFacts.languages: Tibetan (official local), Mandarin (official national), Naxi in southern areas
quickFacts.visaFree: Eligible under China's 240-hour visa-free transit policy (since late 2024); Shangri-La Airport is one of 65 entry ports. 38 countries have 30-day visa-free entry.
quickFacts.internet: VPN required for Google, Instagram, WhatsApp, Facebook, Twitter, YouTube. China-hosted apps (WeChat, Alipay, Dianping, Ctrip) work without VPN.
quickFacts.tapWater: Do NOT drink tap water. Bottled water widely available (¥2-5/bottle).
